review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the cylinder membership lemmas in Parabolic/Basic.lean and Heat/Cylinder.lean. I grepped downstream uses of `centeredBackwardHeatTest` in Core/Caccioppoli. I did not run Lean, so the suggestions are untested. I found no loop or competing-rule problems. The two findings are about missing or private simp interface lemmas. I rate them low to moderate severity. They are based on repeated downstream unfolding, not on observed simp failures.

findings.excerpt:
def centeredBackwardHeatTest (x₀ : Vec3) (t₀ r : ℝ) (z : ParabolicPoint) : ℝ :=
  backwardHeatTestFunction r (z.1 - x₀) (z.2 - t₀)
findings.problem: The definition has no unfolding or simp lemma in the point-evaluation form `centeredBackwardHeatTest x₀ t₀ r z = backwardHeatTestFunction r (z.1 - x₀) (z.2 - t₀)`. It has no such lemma for the gradient-norm variant either. Every consumer unfolds the definition by name with `simpa only [centeredBackwardHeatTest] using …`. This happens four times in this file (lower, upper, annulus and gradient-norm bounds) and again in CaccioppoliEnergy, CaccioppoliEnergyLower, RawI4 and CaccioppoliRHS. Each time the result is converted by hand to the `backwardHeatTestFunction r (w.1 - x₀) (w.2 - t₀)` form. The simp normal form of the centered function is therefore left implicit.
findings.proposed_change: Add an equation lemma such as `theorem centeredBackwardHeatTest_apply (x₀ t₀ r z) : centeredBackwardHeatTest x₀ t₀ r z = backwardHeatTestFunction r (z.1 - x₀) (z.2 - t₀) := rfl`. Add a matching one for `centeredBackwardHeatTestGradientNorm`. Mark them `@[simp]` only if downstream goals should normalize to the `backwardHeatTestFunction` form. Otherwise cite them as `simpa only [centeredBackwardHeatTest_apply]`. Both options give an explicit, stable rewrite direction, and the name `centeredBackwardHeatTest_apply` is a suggestion only. The `rfl` proof is safe because the rewrite is terminating (it only unfolds one definition layer).
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs stop depending on the definition's body. A later change to the definition would then need only one edit. The orientation is documented and uniform across the lower, upper, annulus and gradient bounds.

findings.excerpt:
private lemma mem_parabolicCylinder_sub_center {x₀ : Vec3} {t₀ r : ℝ}
    {z : ParabolicPoint} :
    z ∈ parabolicCylinder x₀ t₀ r ↔
      (z.1 - x₀, z.2 - t₀) ∈ parabolicCylinder 0 0 r
findings.problem: The only simp lemma for cylinder membership is stated for explicit pairs `(y, s) ∈ parabolicCylinder x t r`. For a variable `z : ParabolicPoint` it gives no canonical form for the shifted-to-origin membership. The file works around this with two private, non-simp translation lemmas, one for the cylinder and one for the annulus `Cyl(ρ) \ Cyl(ρ/2)`. Other files that need the same reduction cannot reuse them. Both are used only through explicit `.mp` calls. Nothing normalizes `z ∈ parabolicCylinder x₀ t₀ r` and its centered translate to a common form.
findings.proposed_change: Make the translation lemma public and put it next to `mem_parabolicCylinder` in Parabolic/Basic.lean, with a name that does not clash with existing ones. Also provide a coordinate form for a variable `z`, for example `z ∈ parabolicCylinder x t r ↔ vec3EuclideanNorm (z.1 - x) < r ∧ t - r ^ 2 < z.2 ∧ z.2 ≤ t`, which can be `@[simp]`. The annulus version is already derivable from the cylinder version. Use `Set.mem_diff` and the public translation lemma so that `simp` closes it, and drop the hand-written second private lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated private translation lemmas and gives simp a canonical rewrite for membership of a variable point. Other cylinder files can reuse it without redoing the `linarith` shifts.
